name: Brain On BNB AI — code library
note: No secrets are included in any bundle. They are supplied at runtime through the environment.

bundles.title: Buyback & Burn Bot
bundles.tagline: The bot that has run every ten minutes since launch.

reqs.what: A wallet with a little gas in it
reqs.ours: one BSC wallet, topped up from the tax itself
reqs.alt: the token was launched on four.meme and trades on PancakeSwap V2; the swap calls are the only PancakeSwap-specific part

reqs.what: Somewhere that runs code on a schedule
reqs.ours: a Cloudflare Worker on a 10-minute cron
reqs.alt: a VPS with crontab, GitHub Actions, Fly.io, Railway, a Raspberry Pi, or node on your own machine

reqs.what: Somewhere to keep a small run log
reqs.ours: one Cloudflare KV namespace
reqs.alt: Redis, SQLite, Postgres, or a JSON file on disk — it writes one entry per cycle

reqs.what: A BSC RPC endpoint
reqs.ours: the public endpoints, with failover
reqs.alt: NodeReal, Ankr, QuickNode or your own node if you want the headroom

reqs.what: One secret at runtime: PRIVATE_KEY
reqs.ours: wrangler secret put
reqs.alt: a .env file, your host's secret store — anything but the source code

bundles.title: Dev Sweep Bot
bundles.tagline: The hourly one that empties the tax wallet.

reqs.what: A wallet that receives the tax
reqs.ours: the same wallet the buyback bot spends from
reqs.alt: any wallet — it only needs to be the one your token routes its fee to

reqs.what: Somewhere that runs code hourly
reqs.ours: a Cloudflare Worker on a cron trigger
reqs.alt: crontab, systemd timer, GitHub Actions, or any scheduler you already run

reqs.what: Somewhere to keep a cursor
reqs.ours: one KV namespace, shared with the buyback bot
reqs.alt: a file, a Redis key, a single database row — it stores very little

reqs.what: One secret at runtime: PRIVATE_KEY
reqs.ours: wrangler secret put
reqs.alt: a .env file or your host's secret store

bundles.title: Liquidity Add & LP Burn
bundles.tagline: Adds liquidity, then burns the LP token it just received.

reqs.what: A wallet holding both sides of the pair
reqs.ours: BNB and the token, in one wallet
reqs.alt: any PancakeSwap V2 pair, and any BSC DEX sharing that router interface — the router is one constant

reqs.what: A machine that can run Node 18+
reqs.ours: run by hand, when we decide to add
reqs.alt: put it on a cron if you want it automatic; nothing in it needs a human

reqs.what: Slippage set for a fee-on-transfer token
reqs.alt: none — a normal 1% simply reverts. This is the single thing that breaks naive add-liquidity scripts

reqs.what: One secret at runtime: PRIVATE_KEY
reqs.ours: a local .env file
reqs.alt: your shell environment, a secret manager, a hardware signer

bundles.title: Telegram Bot
bundles.tagline: Buy alerts, burn alerts, price, whale tracking, captcha.

reqs.what: A bot token
reqs.ours: one from @BotFather, two minutes of work
reqs.alt: none — this is Telegram's only door

reqs.what: Somewhere to receive a webhook and run a cron
reqs.ours: a single Cloudflare Worker doing both
reqs.alt: any HTTPS endpoint: a small VPS, Deno Deploy, Vercel, Fly.io. Long-polling works too, at the cost of a process that never sleeps

reqs.what: Somewhere to keep state
reqs.ours: one Cloudflare KV namespace
reqs.alt: Redis, SQLite, Postgres — it stores the block cursor, the watchlist and the captcha queue

reqs.what: A BSC RPC endpoint that allows eth_getLogs
reqs.ours: a keyed endpoint, with free ones as fallback
reqs.alt: NodeReal, Ankr, QuickNode. Note that bsc-dataseed refuses log queries outright

reqs.what: One secret at runtime: BOT_TOKEN
reqs.ours: wrangler secret put
reqs.alt: any secret store your host offers

bundles.title: NFT Auto-Mint Bot
bundles.tagline: Watches the pair and mints to the buyer, unasked.

reqs.what: A deployed ERC-721 it is allowed to mint from
reqs.ours: the contract in the NFT Buy Drops bundle
reqs.alt: any ERC-721 with a mint function and a minter role

reqs.what: A wallet with gas
reqs.ours: the bot pays the mint, so the buyer pays nothing
reqs.alt: you could make the buyer claim and pay — but then it is a claim page, not a drop

reqs.what: Somewhere that runs code on a schedule
reqs.ours: a Cloudflare Worker cron
reqs.alt: crontab, GitHub Actions, any always-on process

reqs.what: Somewhere to keep the block cursor
reqs.ours: one KV namespace
reqs.alt: a file or a database row. Whatever it is, it must be durable: this is what stops a restart double-minting

reqs.what: One secret at runtime: PRIVATE_KEY
reqs.ours: wrangler secret put
reqs.alt: a .env file or your host's secret store

bundles.title: Prize Pool & Payout Bot
bundles.tagline: Filled a prize pool from trading tax, then paid 39 wallets out.

reqs.what: A wallet holding the pool
reqs.ours: a dedicated wallet, funded by a slice of the tax
reqs.alt: a multisig if the pool is large enough to be worth arguing about

reqs.what: Somewhere the entries and scores live
reqs.ours: the Supabase project from the Worldcup bundle
reqs.alt: any Postgres, or any store you can read a winners list out of

reqs.what: A machine that can run Node 18+
reqs.ours: run by hand, watched, one round at a time
reqs.alt: none worth having. This one sends money to strangers — do not put it on a cron

reqs.what: Secrets at runtime: PRIVATE_KEY, database URL and key
reqs.ours: a local .env file
reqs.alt: a secret manager. Never the source

reqs.what: A dry run first
reqs.ours: --dry-run, every single time
reqs.alt: there is no alternative. Read the script before you copy it

bundles.title: Pool Scanner
bundles.tagline: Reads any BNB Chain pool. No backend at all.

reqs.what: A static host
reqs.ours: Cloudflare Pages
reqs.alt: GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, S3, nginx, or python -m http.server on your laptop

reqs.what: Public RPC endpoints
reqs.ours: six, with failover, all free
reqs.alt: your own node if you expect traffic. Note the requests leave from the visitor's browser, not your server — which is why this costs nothing to run

reqs.what: Nothing else
reqs.ours: no backend, no database, no API key, no build step
reqs.alt: that is the whole point of it

bundles.title: NFT Buy Drops
bundles.tagline: The contract, the metadata server and the collection page.

reqs.what: A wallet with gas for the deployment
reqs.ours: one transaction on BSC, a few cents
reqs.alt: any EVM chain — the contract is plain Solidity with no chain-specific parts

reqs.what: Somewhere to serve the metadata
reqs.ours: a small Cloudflare Worker
reqs.alt: static JSON files on any host. It is one file per token id and nothing else

reqs.what: Somewhere to host the images
reqs.ours: our own domain, over plain HTTPS
reqs.alt: IPFS or Arweave — but link them by https gateway. Several marketplaces will not resolve an ipfs:// URL

reqs.what: Your marketplace metadata set BEFORE you renounce
reqs.ours: set, checked, then renounced
reqs.alt: none. After renouncing it is permanent, and no marketplace can help you

bundles.title: Worldcup Tipping Game
bundles.tagline: A full tournament game that paid out on-chain.

reqs.what: A Postgres with row-level security and auth
reqs.ours: Supabase, free tier, all the way through
reqs.alt: any Postgres plus an auth layer. The schema is plain SQL; the RLS policies are the part worth reading

reqs.what: Somewhere that pulls fixtures on a schedule
reqs.ours: a Cloudflare Worker cron
reqs.alt: any scheduler. It fetches, compares and writes — nothing exotic

reqs.what: A fixtures and results feed
reqs.ours: football-data.org, free tier
reqs.alt: any sports API, or type the results in by hand for a small tournament

reqs.what: A wallet, only if you pay out on-chain
reqs.ours: one wallet, one payout script, 39 transactions
reqs.alt: skip it entirely and the game still works — the prize pool is optional scaffolding

bundles.title: Burn & Add Liq — Browser Game
bundles.tagline: One HTML file. Jump, burn, dodge the dumps.

reqs.what: A static host
reqs.ours: Cloudflare Pages
reqs.alt: anything that can serve one HTML file. Open it from disk and it plays

reqs.what: A score table, only if you want the board
reqs.ours: one Supabase table; the SQL is in the bundle
reqs.alt: any database with an HTTP API, or leave it out — the game runs fine and keeps scores locally

reqs.what: To know what a public score table means
reqs.ours: anyone holding the browser key can post a score
reqs.alt: put the insert behind your own endpoint, or add an upper bound, if the board is meant to be competitive

bundles.title: brainScreener
bundles.tagline: Thirteen self-tests. No accounts, no tracking, no backend.

reqs.what: A static host
reqs.ours: Cloudflare Pages
reqs.alt: any of them. There is no build step and no framework

reqs.what: Nothing else
reqs.ours: no database, no accounts, no analytics, no cookies
reqs.alt: the answers never leave the browser, which is a design decision rather than a shortcut

bundles.title: Agent Tools — MCP & llms.txt
bundles.tagline: What an AI agent sees when it asks this project a question.

reqs.what: A machine that can run Node 18+
reqs.ours: the MCP server over stdio, locally
reqs.alt: point any MCP client at it — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or your own

reqs.what: Somewhere to serve the HTTP tools
reqs.ours: the Pages worker already serving the site
reqs.alt: any HTTPS endpoint, or skip it and run the MCP server only

reqs.what: No keys at all
reqs.ours: every tool reads public chain data
reqs.alt: there is nothing to secure here, which is why it can be pointed at an agent without a second thought

bundles.title: The Agent Service — x402, Broker & Census
bundles.tagline: An agent that sells something, and gets paid without a human in the loop.

reqs.what: A wallet to be paid into
reqs.ours: one BSC wallet, separate from the bots
reqs.alt: any address — it is only ever a recipient, and the worker never holds its key

reqs.what: Somewhere that runs code on a schedule
reqs.ours: a Cloudflare Worker, 15-minute cron
reqs.alt: anything with a timer — the cron drives the watch sweep, the daily census and the canary

reqs.what: Somewhere to keep watches and the census
reqs.ours: one KV namespace
reqs.alt: Redis, SQLite, Postgres — it stores one record per watch and one blob per census tick

reqs.what: A payment facilitator, or none
reqs.ours: the public Dexter facilitator for the standard route
reqs.alt: the direct-transfer route needs no facilitator at all, which is why both are offered

reqs.what: A BSC RPC endpoint
reqs.ours: the public endpoints, with failover
reqs.alt: any node — note that some public RPCs cannot serve eth_getTransactionReceipt, which payment verification needs

reqs.what: Two secrets at runtime: X402_WALLET and the admin trigger secret
reqs.ours: wrangler secret put
reqs.alt: the ownership proofs in the catalogue are signed offline and pasted in as constants — the private key never reaches the worker

bundles.title: The Census — reading a whole registry
bundles.tagline: Every agent id on BNB Chain, and every job they were ever paid for.

reqs.what: Node 18+ and time
reqs.ours: about three hours for the registry, twenty minutes for the jobs
reqs.alt: both resume, so it can be run in pieces — the state file is the progress

reqs.what: RPC endpoints
reqs.ours: eleven public BSC nodes in rotation, 25 calls per batch
reqs.alt: any node list. Breadth matters more than speed: each one rate-limits separately, and 40 per batch is refused where 25 goes through

reqs.what: No keys
reqs.ours: every call is a read
reqs.alt: nothing here can move anything, which is why it can be pointed at a stranger’s contract without a second thought
